Neither team has been winning the chance battle. At five on five, SJS has taken 43% of the expected goals (the quality of shots each side creates) and TOR 44%. Both are giving up more than they generate, with SJS at 3.7 expected goals against per 60 minutes and TOR at 3.6. The model sees a close game tonight, 3.31 expected goals for TOR and 3.13 for SJS. The special-teams matchup to watch is the SJS power play, which creates 0.77 expected goals a game, against a TOR penalty kill allowing 0.82.

In net, the projected starters are Yaroslav Askarov for SJS and Sergei Bobrovsky for TOR. Askarov sits at -1.4 goals saved above expected this season (how many goals a goalie stops compared with what the shots would suggest) and -19.4 last season. Bobrovsky is at +2.5 this year after -13.5 last year. Recent form is similar: SJS is 2-2-1 in its last five with 45% of the expected goals, and TOR is 1-2-2 with 46%. TOR is winless in three (0-2-1) and has been outscored 14-9, though the chances say it is mostly bad luck, since the Maple Leafs got 51% of the expected goals in those games. The model doesn't price that, so it's no guarantee of a turnaround. TOR also plays without John Tavares, who is on injured reserve.

For the players to watch, Macklin Celebrini has a 45% chance to score and an 86% chance to record a point, the highest on either side. William Nylander (41% to score) and Auston Matthews (40%) lead TOR, and Aatu Räty could debut after joining from the Canucks. For SJS, it's game three of a six-game road trip, which the Sharks started 1-0-1.
